Current completed status record gives the authoritative official evaluation, artifact file list, protocol validation, timing, and pass counts.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport-only and records prompt completion for the parallel session; no semantic task actions are projected from it.
Session index is transport-only and maps the single parallel session identity; no semantic task actions are projected from it.
Agent 0 probed duplicate and equal node values, self-loops, collapsed graphs, MST behavior, path output, traversal output, and connectivity edge cases, then returned a black-box behavior report.
Agent 1 probed traversal and path ordering, negative and large labels, duplicate values, Dijkstra ties, argparse errors, and returned formatting and ordering rules.
Agent 2 focused on CLI parsing fidelity, including help, required flags, duplicate flags, unknown arguments, equals form, negative values, and exit codes.
Agent 3 implemented graph.mjs and buildGraph, verified duplicate edge updates, self-loops, insertion order, and quotient-of-cycle cases, then returned exported-symbol details.

Agent 4 implemented mst.mjs; it initially could not read graph.mjs, later inspected current modules, wrote stable Kruskal, observed a graph edgeList ordering mismatch in validation, and verified MST against a contract stub.
Agent 5 implemented dijkstra.mjs with strict-less relaxation and discovery-counter tie behavior, then verified source-target, tie, and unreachable cases.
Agent 6 implemented traversal.mjs; after an initial BigInt JSON stringify test failure, it reran formatted BFS/DFS checks that matched the expected ordering.
Agent 7 implemented connectivity.mjs for the constrained graph family and verified connected, disconnected, self-loop, leaf, and isolated-node cases against a local stub.
Agent 8 implemented pyformat.mjs and cli.mjs; one malformed Write call was corrected, and a Node assertion script verified parsing and formatting behavior.

Parallel parent probed the executable, launched exploration and implementation swarms, inspected generated modules, wrote test10.mjs, ran fixed-case diffs, 120 randomized diffs, numeric literal checks, syntax checks, and final response.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport-only and records prompt completion for the serial session; no semantic task actions are projected from it.
Session index is transport-only and maps the single serial session identity; no semantic task actions are projected from it.

Serial main actor probed executable behavior, wrote all library modules and the entry point locally, found and fixed connectivity mismatches, then verified all 52 graph shapes, 40 fuzz cases, equals-form CLI, and error exits.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized that it had to reproduce the networkx script in pure Node ESM .mjs files, parse --a through --e manually, avoid external dependencies and Python, preserve BigInt labels, and match Python output byte-for-byte.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent used two AgentSwarm rounds: three exploration children for black-box behavior and six coder children for graph, MST, Dijkstra, traversal, connectivity, formatting, and CLI modules; the parent kept assembly and final acceptance.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote separate modules under /output/lib and /output/lib/algorithms; the parent then wrote /output/test10.mjs importing those local modules and matching the print order.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After the implementation swarm returned, the parent read the generated modules, composed the entry file, ran differential checks, and delivered the final /output tree listed in its final response.
parallel.verification: Parallel verified baseline and representative degenerate cases, 120 randomized differential cases including huge integers, numeric literal cases such as +007 and whitespace, and node --check for all generated files.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished delivered behavior remained in official evaluation; a graph edgeList order concern and minor child-local test/tool issues were observed but the final artifact passed all 160 official tests.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Node ESM, .mjs, manual argparse-compatible CLI, no external dependency, black-box NetworkX behavior, and byte-for-byte output obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main actor owned probing, all module implementations, the entry point, tests, connectivity repair, and closure without child delegation.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote graph, mst, dijkstra, traversal, connectivity, pyformat, args, and test10 modules, then replaced connectivity.mjs after fuzzing exposed NetworkX self-loop-heavy connectivity behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor wrote all files, integration was direct through local imports in test10.mjs and final artifacts were summarized from the same trajectory.
serial.verification: Serial checked fixed cases, inspected mismatch output, ran all 52 canonical equality patterns, ran 40 randomized cases, verified equals-form arguments, and confirmed invalid/missing argument exit code 2.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The initial connectivity implementation was wrong for self-loop-heavy graphs, but the serial actor diagnosed and patched it before closure; official evaluation passed 160/160.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM .mjs, manual CLI, pure JavaScript, no external dependency, BigInt label, and exact output parity obligations, then encoded them into child contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and treated exact command-line and NetworkX-output compatibility as the governing requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage gap remained; parallel externalized requirements into swarm briefs while serial carried them in one trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first delegated three probe scopes and then six non-overlapping module scopes, with the parent retaining the entry-file and final verification role.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership in the main actor, writing graph, MST, Dijkstra, traversal, connectivity, formatting, args, and entry files itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used file-scoped child ownership and parent assembly; serial used one continuous implementation owner for all modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried explicit cross-module APIs for Graph, MST, Dijkstra, traversal, connectivity, formatting, and CLI so separately written files could compose.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained interface knowledge locally and adjusted module behavior after observing concrete mismatches in its own verification loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel relied on transferred contracts and later inspection; serial relied on single-context continuity and local repair.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children implemented separate graph, algorithm, formatting, and CLI modules, and the parent composed test10.mjs using those modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all modules and the entry point directly, then replaced connectivity.mjs after discovering NetworkX self-loop behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced modular implementations, but parallel assembled child outputs while serial iterated locally on an initially wrong connectivity implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel collected AgentSwarm results, inspected the produced files, noticed the reported edgeList concern, and still verified the composed solution against the executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; its results were local writes, test outputs, background task output, and subsequent edits inside one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a completed child-result join and inspection step; serial had direct local iteration without child handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct files in /output; the parent read the modules and wrote the entry point that imported the local .mjs files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote every file itself under /output and used a flatter library layout with local imports from test10.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared a workspace but partitioned writes by file; serial avoided cross-agent shared-state risk by using one writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified baseline and degenerate diffs, ran 120 randomized differential cases including huge integers, checked numeric literal cases, and syntax-checked all generated files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified all 52 canonical equality patterns, 40 wider fuzz cases, equals-form arguments, and error exit codes after repairing connectivity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached strong evaluator-aligned verification; serial used exhaustive graph-shape coverage, while parallel used broader randomized differential coverage plus syntax checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed more agent time and tokens with 9 subagents, but the agent completed normally and official evaluation later passed 160/160.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used fewer requests and no subagents, completed normally after local repair, and official evaluation also passed 160/160.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was costlier but did not time out or leave unfinished work; serial was more economical with the same official outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 160/160, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is process: parallel obtained behavior facts and module implementations through child agents, then parent-assembled and tested the deliverable; serial implemented and repaired the same behavior in one trajectory after local differential failures. The different workflows converged on accepted solutions.
parallel_contributors: Exploration and coder subagents provided targeted NetworkX behavior rules and separate modules that the parent assembled and tested successfully.
serial_contributors: The single serial actor preserved local context and used exhaustive equality-pattern testing to repair the connectivity edge case before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial had an ordinary local connectivity defect before repair; parallel had a child-observed graph edgeList contract concern, but neither persisted into the official artifact.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both strategies produced accepted solutions with different process costs and verification paths
